episode_title: 24. The Relationship Doesn't Open the Deal Anymore: Curran Ethridge on Digital-First HVAC Buying

real_qa.q: Why has the buying process in commercial HVAC shifted away from rep-driven initial contact?
real_qa.r: The workforce is aging and taking institutional knowledge with them, while buying audiences are becoming more sophisticated and researching digitally before contacting reps. Buyers now do most of their homework before picking up the phone—visiting websites, competitor sites, trade publications, LinkedIn, Reddit, and using AI—forming an impression of who you are before ever calling. The relationship used to open the deal, but now digital opens it and the rep closes it.
real_qa.requete: why commercial HVAC buyers no longer rely on rep relationships

real_qa.q: What percentage of B2B buyers avoid speaking with sales representatives?
real_qa.r: According to a Gartner study, 67% of B2B buyers don't even want to deal with a rep. Additionally, buyers look at an average of six competitors before contacting a manufacturer, and two-thirds of buyers conduct their research online before speaking to anybody.
real_qa.requete: Gartner B2B buyers avoid sales representatives percentage

real_qa.q: How should manufacturers address the shift from relationship-first to digital-first selling in HVAC?
real_qa.r: Companies need to wire digital and relationship strategies together, using digital to educate, qualify, and eliminate friction so that reps arrive at already-warm, educated buyers. Digital presence must answer three core questions: will it work, will you support it, and why should I care—all in plain language without requiring human contact. This scales relationships and reduces wasted motion, allowing every relationship to start from a position of strength.
real_qa.requete: how to implement digital-first HVAC sales strategy with reps

real_qa.q: What friction points cause Generation Z buyers to abandon HVAC manufacturers during evaluation?
real_qa.r: New buyers treat friction as a disqualifier—if they cannot self-educate, if the site doesn't answer their question, if case studies bury insights after 12 pages, or if they must talk to a human just to determine fit, they leave for competitors. Silence and friction signal that a company isn't serious, even if the product is best in category. They evaluate and form opinions before raising their hand, so by the time they contact you, they've already decided based on digital experience.
real_qa.requete: Generation Z HVAC buyer friction disqualifiers digital experience

real_qa.q: Why does using identical messaging across HVAC competitor websites harm a manufacturer's competitive positioning?
real_qa.r: When website copy from five or six competitors reads identically, strangers cannot differentiate between them—and that is exactly what technical buyers experience. Using the same aspirational words like 'innovative' across 90% of industry homepages means you sound the same as seven competitors, which fails to build trust. AI adoption in marketing amplifies this problem because it doesn't instill confidence when you're indistinguishable from your next competitor.
real_qa.requete: HVAC manufacturer website messaging differentiation competitor analysis
